newsitem.title: USA: Governor asks Georgia school board to resign.
newsitem.headline: Governor asks Georgia school board to resign.

text.p: Georgia Gov Zell Miller sent the state Board of Education a letter asking the entire panel to resign, Atlanta Journal and Constitution reported Thursday.
Miller said the resignation of all 10 board members would be the only way to end bickering between the panel and state school Superintendent Linda Schrenko, who must answer to the board.

"It's just a fact that this board and the superintendent cannot work together," Miller wrote in a letter to board memebers Wednesday. "The only way to correct this state of affairs, I have concluded, is simply to start over."
One board member did resign -- Schrenko's longtime pastor, Rev. Ed Floyd.
Board Chairman J.T. Williams told the newspaper he would consult with legislative and education leaders.

"If it's going to help education I'm going to resign immediately," Williams told the paper. "But I don't want to leave everything in chaos...The governor does not have all the facts or he would not be making such a recommendation."

Miller, a Democrat, appointed the board members but cannot force them to resign. Schrenko, a Republican, was elected last year to serve as head of the state Education Department. She and the Democratically controlled school board have been locked in battle over teacher pay raises, block grant funding proposals, and ways to improve test scores.
